plan.title: Liver treated vs control DE with strandedness QC
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples with raw STAR/featureCounts gene-level integer counts (12000 genes x 6 samples), single batch, unpaired. Two problems are flagged before any test: the library strandedness was never recorded, and the counter's strand setting is therefore unverified, which can silently drop or misassign reads for antisense-overlapping gene pairs; and the user doubts the counts are correct. Because raw reads/BAMs are not available in this environment (only the finished count matrix), a true RSeQC infer_experiment run against aligned reads is not possible here — instead we run the closest matroskeeper check achievable from the count matrix itself: examine count-matrix-level signatures of a wrong strand setting (systematic loss of counts genome-wide relative to typical liver depth, anomalous ratios in known antisense-overlapping gene pairs looked up from Ensembl gene models, and consistency of sex-linked/liver-marker gene detection), and report this as a caveat rather than a resolved QC pass. QC also covers general sample structure (PCA, sample-distance heatmap, library size), which independently surfaces gross count problems (a mislabeled or bad sample) the user's doubt calls out. Differential expression follows the grounded DESeq2 procedure (Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, median-of-ratios normalization, minimal pre-filter, BH-adjusted independent filtering at alpha 0.05), with an edgeR quasi-likelihood run in parallel as a robustness cross-check — required because n=3 per group is a low-power design and a two-tool overlap softens the risk that a single tool's borderline calls are noise. Enrichment runs fgsea preranked GSEA on the Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark (primary) and Reactome (secondary), both staged for human. The final report states the replicate-count power ceiling, the strandedness caveat, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, and full reproducibility metadata, so a reader cannot mistake either the gene list or the pathway hits as more certain than a 3-vs-3 design with an unverified strand setting supports.
